Title: Diagnosis of test `org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilderAppendInsertTest.testLang299()`

Details:
The test creates a `StrBuilder` instance with an initial capacity of 1 and then calls `appendFixedWidthPadRight("foo", 1, '-')` on it. The test likely fails because the internal buffer or the method logic does not handle this scenario correctly.

Analysis of the `appendFixedWidthPadRight(Object obj, int width, char padChar)` method:
- The method first ensures the buffer has a capacity at least `size + width`. 
- It converts the given object `obj` to string `str`.
- It gets the length of the string `strLen`.
- If the string length is greater or equal to the width, it uses `str.getChars(0, strLen, buffer, size)` to copy the whole string to internal buffer starting at offset `size`.
- Otherwise, it copies the string and pads with the `padChar` up to `width`.
- Finally, it increments `size` by `width`.

The problem occurs because when `width` is smaller than the string length (in this case, width=1, string length=3), it still copies `strLen` characters (3) into the buffer starting at `size`, which will overflow or overwrite beyond the assumed width space.

The constructor `StrBuilder(int initialCapacity)` initializes the buffer with length equal to initial capacity (1), so the buffer length is 1 initially.

In `appendFixedWidthPadRight`, `ensureCapacity(size + width)` will try to ensure capacity is `size + width`, but `getChars(0, strLen, buffer, size)` still copies 3 characters starting at `size`. This causes buffer overflow or writing beyond the capacity.

Thus, the bug lies in `appendFixedWidthPadRight` where if the string length exceeds the fixed width, the copy operation writes `strLen` characters instead of limiting it to `width`.

Recommended fix:
- Change the call `str.getChars(0, strLen, buffer, size);` to only copy up to `width` characters when `strLen >= width`.

Next, I will check the exact existing lines 883-885 corresponding to the problematic condition to confirm.
